summary: Seiren Matsunami was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1927–1930) and under Walther Schubring (~1937–1940). He held professorships at Kyushu University (~1950–1967) and Rissho University (~1967–1974).

Seishi Karashima specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University under mentors including Minoru Hara, K. R. Norman, and Xianlin Ji. He served as professor at Soka University (~1996–2019).

Seishin Kato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1888–1891) and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He lectured at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1923) and served as president of Buzan University (1918, 1923), Taisho University (1940), and Toyo University (1952, 1955).
Seitatsu Matsunami worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

Seizan Yanagida specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto universities under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Kaiten Nukariya. He held faculty posts at Hanazono University (1949–1996), Kyoto University (1976–1986), and Chubu University (~1988–1997).
Sen Wang was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Peking University (~1932–1936) and served as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1952–1964).

Senarat Wijayasundara worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. His career included teaching at the University of Kelaniya and serving as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore (both attested 1999).
Senarath Paranavitana worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe and held a post at Leiden University.

Senchu Murano was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University (~1930–1933) and the University of Washington (~1934–1938), later serving as a professor at Rissho University (~1957–1978).

Sengaku Mayeda specialized in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under W. Norman Brown at the University of Pennsylvania. He held faculty posts at Pennsylvania, the University of Tokyo (1973; 1982–1991), and Musashino University.

Senkyo Sakawa specialized in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Rissho University (graduating 1965), where he later served as professor of Buddhist studies (attested 1981–1985) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Senmyo Naniwa worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University, studying under P. V. Bapat, Genjun Sasaki, M. G. Dhadphale, and J. R. Joshi. He held posts at Bukkyo University and Toho Kenkyukai (both attested 2005).
Sensho Kimura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Otani University (~1962–1970) and later served there as a professor (~1982–2013).

Sensho Murakami was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, Takakura Gakuryo, and Toyo University. He taught at Toyo University (~1887–1900), Otani University (1926–1928), and the University of Tokyo (1888; 1901–1923), where he became professor.
Sentaro Sawamura was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1907–1910) and later held an academic post there (~1920–1930).

Seok-hyeong Kim worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University (~1928–1931), later serving as a lecturer at Seoul National University and as a professor at Dongguk University.

Seong-Uk Kim specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr. and serves as Cho Associate Professor in Korean Culture and Religion at Columbia University (attested 2026).
Ser Kha Chödrak pursued his studies under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Sergey Malov was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Academy and St. Petersburg University under Nikolai Katanov. He held posts at Kazan Federal University (~1917–1922) and the National Library of Russia (1931–1933).

Sergey Oldenburg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ivan Minayev at Saint Petersburg State University. He became professor there (1889, 1894), led the Russian Academy of Sciences (1904–1929), and directed the Asiatic Museum (1916–1930).
